artworks.title: Demeter and Metanira (Eleusinian hydria)
artworks.description: Berlin hydria of the Eleusinian mysteries: Demeter with Metanira — queen of the household Homeric Hymn names as Celeus' wife. The vase stages the palace where the disguised goddess nursed Demophon and taught the rites.

artworks.title: Demeter, Persephone, and Triptolemus (Eleusis relief)
artworks.description: The great Eleusis votive (NAMA 126): Triptolemus receives Demeter's wheat — the son traditions give to Celeus, king of Eleusis, as the envoy who carries agriculture from his father's city to the world.

popCulture.title: Homeric Hymn to Demeter
popCulture.description: The hymn makes Celeus the Eleusinian king who hosts Demeter — husband of Metanira, father of Demophon and the daughters who bring the goddess indoors.

popCulture.title: Celeus
popCulture.description: Mythical king of Eleusis — host of Demeter in the Homeric Hymn; father of Triptolemus and Demophon in the lineages that fix the Mysteries' founding household.

popCulture.title: Eleusinian Mysteries
popCulture.description: The rites Demeter taught in Celeus' Eleusis — the king's hospitality rewritten as the origin of Greece's most secret agrarian cult.
